cohort: The study cohort comprised 532 births to women with a lifetime eating disorder diagnosis and 43,657 births to non-ED women, identified through linked hospital patient registers, population-based data (The HUNT Study), and the Medical Birth Registry in Norway.
finding: Lifetime history of eating disorders was associated with specific adverse obstetric outcomes: anorexia nervosa with SGA, bulimia nervosa with Caesarean section, and EDNOS/sub-threshold ED with low 5-min Apgar score.
mod_finding: Women with a lifetime history of bulimia nervosa had higher odds of having a Caesarean section (OR 1.7 95% CI 1.1-2.5).
